questions.question: An insurance company's Power Automate-based claims processing flow is experiencing intermittent failures when connecting to a downstream policy management system. The failures occur during peak load and cause incomplete claims records. The system has no retry logic or fallback path configured. Which Power Platform Well-Architected pillar is primarily being violated, and what should the architect recommend?
options: A. Reliability — add retry policies and configure redundant connectors with failover paths
B. Operational Excellence — implement ALM with Azure DevOps
C. Security — apply DLP policies to prevent connector exposure
D. Performance Efficiency — offload tasks to Azure Functions
questions.explanation: Peak-load intermittent failures with no retry/fallback are a Reliability pillar concern. Add retry policies and redundant connectors with failover paths.
questions.topic: Well-Architected / Reliability

questions.question: A business unit requests urgent deployment of a custom connector that integrates an external market intelligence vendor into Copilot for Dynamics 365 Sales. The connector is built and tested, but the legal team has not reviewed the third-party vendor's privacy policy or data terms. The business sponsor insists on a same-week launch. What should the architect recommend?
options: A. Certify the connector organization-wide to streamline the compliance review process
B. Enable the connector in the dev environment only until legal review is complete
C. Delay deployment until legal and compliance review of the external data source is completed
D. Deploy the connector immediately and schedule the legal review for post-launch
questions.explanation: External data source integrations require legal/compliance review of privacy terms before deployment, regardless of deadline pressure.
questions.topic: Governance / Compliance

questions.question: According to agent design best practices, when a knowledge source has not yet finished processing, what should the architect do before publishing?
options: A. Publish the agent immediately to meet the deadline and patch any knowledge issues post-deployment
B. Publish the agent with a disclaimer to users that knowledge may be incomplete
C. Wait for the knowledge source to show "Ready," perform scenario-based testing, and then publish
D. Replace the new documents with an older version that already has a Ready status
questions.explanation: Wait for the knowledge source to reach Ready, then do scenario-based testing before publishing.
questions.topic: Agent Design / Knowledge Grounding

questions.question: TRUE or FALSE: "Prompt injection vulnerabilities only affect public-facing AI agents and do not require mitigation controls in internal enterprise AI agents used by authenticated employees."
options: A. True
B. False
questions.explanation: Prompt injection affects internal agents too; mitigation controls are required regardless of audience.
questions.topic: Security / Prompt Injection

questions.question: A global pharmaceutical company needs a conversational AI agent to assist regulatory compliance officers. The process involves highly proprietary compound data, strict FDA-governed decision workflows, and internal IP that cannot be shared with any external vendor. The organization has a mature AI engineering team. Which AI development approach should the architect recommend?
options: A. Build — Develop a fully custom AI solution to maintain data control and regulatory compliance
B. Buy — Use a prebuilt Microsoft 365 Copilot solution to accelerate time-to-value
C. Extend — Use Azure AI Foundry with a fine-tuned model connected to SharePoint
D. Extend — Customize Copilot Studio with grounding documents from SharePoint
questions.explanation: Highly proprietary IP that cannot leave the org, strict regulatory workflows, and a mature AI team favor Build (fully custom).
questions.topic: Build/Buy/Extend Decision

questions.question: A government agency is deploying a Copilot Studio agent for benefits enrollment. All user questions follow predictable, structured patterns defined by a legal mandate. The agency requires deterministic responses with no generative behavior to meet audit requirements. Which language understanding approach should the architect configure?
options: A. Generative AI orchestration — to handle open-ended user queries dynamically
B. Standard NLU — for strict intent matching with deterministic, non-generative responses
C. Azure CLU — to support multilingual intent recognition across varied phrasing
D. NLU Boost with generative answers — to answer questions from internal SharePoint knowledge
questions.explanation: Deterministic, non-generative, audit-friendly responses call for Standard NLU with strict intent matching.
questions.topic: Copilot Studio / Language Understanding

questions.question: A public-facing AI customer support agent for a bank allows users to upload PDF attachments. During red team testing, attackers embedded hidden override instructions within uploaded PDFs, steering the agent to bypass its system-level safety instructions and return restricted account information. What is the MOST effective mitigation the architect should implement?
options: A. Disable PDF upload support entirely to eliminate the attack vector
B. Add CAPTCHA verification to the upload form to ensure only human users can submit files
C. Strengthen input and output filtering — strip unsafe embedded content and HTML from inputs, limit accepted file types, apply safety filters on model outputs, and block code execution attempts
D. Enable daily manual review of all uploaded files by a security analyst
questions.explanation: Layered input/output filtering (strip embedded content, limit file types, output safety filters, block code execution) is the most effective mitigation.
questions.topic: Security / Content Safety

questions.question: An insurance company is designing a multi-agent claims processing solution. The workflow requires: (1) extracting claim details, (2) translating foreign-language documents, (3) running a QA validation on completeness, and (4) routing to the appropriate team. Each step must complete before the next begins, and any failure must halt the pipeline. Which orchestration pattern should the architect select?
options: A. Handoff orchestration, so each agent decides independently who to route to next.
B. Concurrent orchestration, so all agents process in parallel to reduce latency.
C. Sequential orchestration, where each agent processes in a deterministic stage-by-stage pipeline.
D. Group chat orchestration, so agents negotiate the task sequence dynamically.
questions.explanation: Dependent stages that must complete in order and halt on failure map to Sequential orchestration.
questions.topic: Multi-Agent Orchestration

questions.question: An enterprise AI agent in a legal firm operates in two modes: it retrieves case documents on behalf of a logged-in attorney during active sessions, and it performs overnight background batch analysis without user interaction. A developer proposes using a single elevated service account for both modes. What is the correct authorization architecture?
options: A. Use a single managed identity scoped to the highest-permission level so both modes always succeed
B. Propagate the attorney's permissions when the agent acts on their behalf; use a narrowly scoped service role when the agent acts as itself for background batch processing
C. Use a single elevated service account with full permissions to cover both operating modes
D. Use OAuth client credentials for all modes to standardize authentication across both scenarios
questions.explanation: On-behalf-of should propagate user permissions; autonomous background work should use a narrowly scoped service role (least privilege).
questions.topic: Identity / Authorization

questions.question: A solution architect is beginning the ALM design for a new AI-powered sentiment detection feature in Dynamics 365 Customer Service. The development team is eager to start building prompts and configuring conversation boosters. What should the architect do FIRST?
options: A. Build prompts for sentiment classification and configure conversation boosters in Copilot
B. Package and version the agent assets inside a solution file using semantic versioning
C. Define AI use cases, required data sources, customer data flows, sensitivity labels, and compliance constraints
D. Set up environment variables for connectors, API endpoints, and knowledge indices
questions.explanation: Governance-first: define use cases, data sources, data flows, sensitivity labels, and compliance constraints before building.
questions.topic: ALM / Planning

questions.question: An organization is designing a governance framework for a Copilot agent that handles sensitive HR compensation data. The HR Director proposes using a shared cloud identity across DEV, TEST, and PROD to reduce identity management overhead. What is the architect's correct guidance?
options: A. Assign a unique cloud identity per agent per environment — DEV, PRE-PROD, and PROD — recording ownership, version, and lifecycle metadata for each
B. Use a shared identity but restrict its permissions to read-only in non-production environments
C. Accept the shared identity model and apply environment-specific DLP policies to compensate for the risk
D. Allow the shared identity between DEV and TEST only, with a separate identity for PROD
questions.explanation: Unique identity per agent per environment with ownership/version/lifecycle metadata; never share identities across environments.
questions.topic: Governance / Identity

questions.question: TRUE or FALSE: "In a governed enterprise Copilot for Service deployment, human review before sending externally generated content is unnecessary overhead when the model produces high-quality summaries."
options: A. True
B. False
questions.explanation: Human review before external send remains required in governed deployments; it cannot be removed for speed.
questions.topic: Responsible AI / Human-in-the-Loop

questions.question: [Case Study - CHG] A proposed Patient Intake Agent automatically commits patient records, uses generative responses, has no human approval checkpoints, and includes no content safety controls. Statement: "This design is acceptable because built-in Copilot safeguards are sufficient for regulated healthcare workloads."
options: A. True
B. False
questions.explanation: Built-in safeguards are not sufficient for regulated HIPAA workloads; auto-commit + generative + no human approval + no content safety is unacceptable.
questions.topic: Responsible AI / Regulated Workloads

questions.question: A financial services organization wants to automate 40% of its manual loan-processing data entry using a Copilot Studio agent. The sponsor estimates a 60% productivity gain, but there is no baseline of current processing time and no usage telemetry. What should you do FIRST before building a ROI business case?
options: A. Proceed to design the agent and collect ROI data during the pilot phase
B. Establish a baseline by measuring current task time, volume, and error rates before modeling ROI
C. Request Copilot Studio licensing immediately to access ROI analytics dashboards
D. Submit the ROI projections using industry benchmark data since no internal data exists
questions.explanation: Establish a measured baseline (task time, volume, error rates) before modeling ROI.
questions.topic: Business Value / ROI

questions.question: [Case Study - CHG] CHG has inconsistent AI outputs across departments due to fragmented data sources and lack of unified business definitions. A proposal suggests relying only on existing data models and Copilot capabilities. Statement: "This approach will provide consistent and governed cross-domain reasoning for CHG."
options: A. True
B. False
questions.explanation: Fragmented data and missing unified definitions cannot yield consistent, governed cross-domain reasoning by relying only on existing models.
questions.topic: Data Foundation / Governance

questions.question: A retail organization wants an autonomous agent in Copilot Studio to automatically process customer refund requests: access order records, calculate refund eligibility, and execute refund transactions in the ERP system — all without human approval. What is the MOST critical architectural risk the architect must address before deploying?
options: A. The agent lacks sufficient trigger configuration for scheduled events
B. The agent cannot be published to Microsoft Teams without admin approval
C. The agent has unrestricted action permissions that violate the principle of least privilege
D. The agent may not support enough knowledge sources to ground responses
questions.explanation: Autonomous financial actions with broad permissions violate least privilege — the most critical risk.
questions.topic: Security / Least Privilege

questions.question: TRUE or FALSE: "Once an AI agent reaches a high success rate, architects can safely reduce monitoring to ad-hoc reviews and focus improvement cycles only when issues are escalated by users."
options: A. True
B. False
questions.explanation: Continuous monitoring is required even with high success rates; you cannot drop to ad-hoc reviews.
questions.topic: Operations / Monitoring

questions.question: Statement: "When building an executive ROI business case for an AI agent, a solution architect should present only the expected-case savings projection, since conservative and optimistic bands add unnecessary complexity for stakeholders."
options: A. True
B. False
questions.explanation: ROI cases should present ranges (conservative/expected/optimistic), not only the expected case.
questions.topic: Business Value / ROI

questions.question: An enterprise architect is designing a Teams-based AI agent to let team members retrieve project documents, summarize recent channel discussions, and automate task creation from messages. Which grounding approach should the architect establish FIRST?
options: A. Use Microsoft Graph as the primary retrieval engine to maximize cross-tenant content coverage
B. Use Azure Blob Storage to host project documents and expose them via a custom connector
C. Enable external web search to supplement any missing project information gaps
D. Use SharePoint sites as the primary knowledge source, ensuring content is well-structured and tagged
questions.explanation: Establish SharePoint as the primary, well-structured/tagged knowledge source first.
questions.topic: Knowledge Grounding / M365

questions.question: An enterprise is deploying a generative AI agent using Microsoft Foundry. The agent must call three external APIs for product pricing, inventory, and shipping. Security mandates that no sensitive customer data is stored persistently and all API calls are restricted to approved domains. Which combination of constraints should the architect enforce?
options: A. Define ephemeral memory policy, implement least-privilege permissions per tool, and restrict external tool calls to allow-listed domains.
B. Use public networking for all API calls to reduce latency, and set connector scoping to maximum to ensure comprehensive data retrieval.
C. Store all interactions in Dataverse for auditability and open API gateway access to all third-party domains.
D. Enable persistent message logging for audit purposes, grant broad API access to improve agent performance, and apply Azure Content Safety.
questions.explanation: Ephemeral memory (no persistent PII) + least privilege per tool + allow-listed domains satisfies all constraints.
questions.topic: Foundry / Security Constraints

questions.question: A logistics company asks its architect to build a multi-agent system with seven specialized agents in the first sprint. The team has moderate AI skills. The architect finds routing and dispatch can cover 80% of the business value independently. What is the most architecturally sound decision?
options: A. Delay the full multi-agent design and first validate a single-agent or two-agent solution covering routing and dispatch, scaling only after validating complexity drivers.
B. Immediately deploy using Foundry with a sequential orchestration pipeline across all seven agents.
C. Use Copilot Studio for all seven agents simultaneously to benefit from rapid, low-code deployment.
D. Accept the seven-agent design, as multi-agent systems provide better modularity and future-proofing.
questions.explanation: Start small (routing+dispatch = 80% value), validate complexity drivers, then scale.
questions.topic: Solution Scoping

questions.question: A manufacturing company has three Copilot agents in production. During review, the Analytics Coach shows an 88% success rate, 3.2-second average response time, and 21 logged issues — the lowest performer. The product owner requests an immediate fix. What should the architect do FIRST?
options: A. Disable the Analytics Coach temporarily to prevent further issue accumulation
B. Escalate to the vendor and request model replacement
C. Review conversation transcripts and telemetry to identify root cause categories driving the failures
D. Immediately update the knowledge files and republish the agent
questions.explanation: Root-cause via transcripts and telemetry before taking corrective action.
questions.topic: Operations / Diagnostics

questions.question: A professional services firm wants to deploy Microsoft 365 Copilot for Sales. Pre-deployment validation reveals several CRM opportunity fields are incomplete and SharePoint sales documents lack sensitivity labels. The business owner wants to roll out within a week. What must the architect complete FIRST?
options: A. Configure Power Automate flows to automate proposal drafting workflows
B. Ensure CRM fields are complete, standardized, and SharePoint documents have proper sensitivity labels applied
C. Enable Copilot for Sales licenses and proceed with a limited pilot
D. Map seller roles to Dynamics 365 opportunity records and test email summarization
questions.explanation: Data readiness first: complete/standardized CRM fields and sensitivity labels on documents.
questions.topic: Copilot for Sales / Data Readiness

questions.question: A pharmaceutical company needs an AI model to classify drug interaction reports with high accuracy. Data is highly domain-specific, regulatory restrictions prevent data from leaving a sovereign region, and response latency must be under 200ms. IT budget is moderate. Which model architecture decision is most appropriate?
options: A. Deploy a customized Small Language Model (SLM) trained on domain-specific data, hosted within the sovereign region.
B. Use a general-purpose LLM via Azure OpenAI, as it provides the best reasoning capability across complex documents.
C. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot with a custom knowledge base of drug interaction documents.
D. Build a multi-agent system where one agent retrieves documents and another classifies them using a general LLM.
questions.explanation: Domain-specific + sovereign residency + low latency + moderate budget favor a customized SLM hosted in-region.
questions.topic: Model Selection / SLM

questions.question: After deploying an enterprise AI agent, the operations team reports severe alert fatigue. All logs — routine access, low-level debug traces, cost events, and critical security anomalies — route into a single alerting channel, and important security signals are being missed. What should the architect redesign?
options: A. Move all logs to a third-party SIEM and let the security team manage all routing independently
B. Disable all non-critical alerts and retain only system downtime notifications
C. Reduce log verbosity to errors only and suppress informational and debug-level events
D. Build dedicated dashboards for quality, safety, and cost; configure alerts specifically for anomalies and budget thresholds; and route security alerts to SOC workflows for triage and escalation
questions.explanation: Separate dashboards per concern, targeted alerts, and SOC routing for security signals.
questions.topic: Observability / Alerting

questions.question: A government agency deploys an AI agent that assists officers in reviewing case files and producing preliminary recommendations. Governance mandates that no AI system makes final decisions autonomously. Which control best enforces the mandate?
options: A. Use Azure AI Content Safety to block any output that contains decision language.
B. Add a disclaimer in the agent's welcome message stating it does not make final decisions.

C. Define explicit behavior envelopes in the agent configuration ("Agent may summarize and recommend; Agent may not decide or execute case outcomes"), combined with mandatory human-in-the-loop checkpoints for high-impact actions.
D. Configure the agent with lower model temperature to reduce confidence in outputs.
questions.explanation: Explicit behavior envelopes plus mandatory human-in-the-loop checkpoints enforce the no-autonomous-decision mandate.
questions.topic: Governance / Guardrails

questions.question: TRUE or FALSE: "Consolidating DEV and TEST into a single shared AI development environment is an acceptable cost-optimization strategy that does not compromise ALM governance integrity."
options: A. True
B. False
questions.explanation: Consolidating DEV/TEST compromises ALM governance integrity; keep environments separate.
questions.topic: ALM / Environments

questions.question: A manufacturing company wants a Copilot Studio autonomous agent to manage supplier follow-up workflows: send reminders to overdue suppliers, update ERP records, and escalate unresolved cases. According to agent design best practices, what should the architect do FIRST?
options: A. Configure event triggers for all inbound supplier communications
B. Connect all ERP tables as knowledge sources to maximize agent context
C. Start with one high-value, well-scoped workflow before expanding agent scope
D. Deploy the agent to Microsoft Teams for user acceptance testing immediately
questions.explanation: Start with one high-value, well-scoped workflow before expanding scope.
questions.topic: Agent Design / Scoping

questions.question: A healthcare company's Copilot for Service agent generates case resolution summaries automatically sent to patients via Power Automate with no human review. Compliance flagged this as a violation. The business team argues removing review improves resolution speed by 40%. What action should the architect take?
options: A. Restrict the Copilot model to reduce verbosity of summaries so risk exposure is minimized
B. Disable all automated flows until the vendor provides compliance certification for the Copilot model
C. Enable DLP policies to intercept outbound messages after they are generated
D. Require human review before any externally generated Copilot content is sent to patients, and update the automation governance guardrails accordingly
questions.explanation: Require human review before external patient-facing content and update governance guardrails.
questions.topic: Responsible AI / Human-in-the-Loop

questions.question: A financial services AI agent processing loan applications is flagged by the SOC for unusual inference patterns — returning unexpected data fragments and potentially exposing customer PII. The incident is unconfirmed but escalating rapidly. A business manager suggests waiting 24 hours. What should the architect do FIRST?
options: A. Disable the compromised model endpoint, preserve inference logs and model artifacts for forensic analysis, and initiate rollback procedures to restore the prior model version
B. Notify the Data Protection Officer and wait for their formal guidance before taking any technical action
C. Re-run all recent prompts against the previous model version to compare output differences
D. Increase monitoring verbosity on the agent and wait 24 hours to determine whether the pattern stabilizes
questions.explanation: Contain first: disable endpoint, preserve forensic evidence, roll back to the prior model version.

questions.question: A bank deploys an autonomous Copilot agent that automatically approves or denies personal loan applications based on AI-generated credit assessments. options: A. Security and Inclusiveness
B. Reliability and Privacy
C. Fairness and Inclusiveness
D. Transparency and Accountability
questions.explanation: No explanation (Transparency) and no human review/ownership of decisions (Accountability).
questions.topic: Responsible AI / Principles

questions.question: A large enterprise has 12 AI use case proposals submitted to the AI Center of Excellence. The CoE has limited capacity, and the executive sponsor wants to approve all 12 for simultaneous execution. According to Microsoft's AI CoE framework, what should the AI CoE do FIRST?
options: A. Begin delivering all 12 using Copilot Studio to minimize risk through the platform's built-in safeguards.
B. Evaluate each use case for business value, technical feasibility, risk level, and organizational readiness before prioritizing a subset for execution.
C. Approve all 12 and assign a governance lead to each project to ensure oversight.
D. Escalate to the legal team to validate compliance for all 12 simultaneously.
questions.explanation: Evaluate and prioritize use cases by value, feasibility, risk, and readiness before execution.

questions.question: A logistics company is building a multi-agent AI system in Azure AI Foundry handling three task types: simple package status lookups, moderately complex route optimization queries, and highly complex supply chain disruption analysis. How should the architect configure the model router to balance cost and performance?
options: A. Use static routing rules: SLM for simple tasks, fine-tuned model for moderate tasks, LLM for complex tasks
B. Route all three task types to a single GPT-4 LLM for consistency
C. Route all tasks to an SLM to reduce token costs uniformly
D. Use weighted routing to distribute all tasks equally across all available models
questions.explanation: Match model capability to task complexity: SLM for simple, fine-tuned for moderate, LLM for complex.
questions.topic: Foundry / Model Routing

questions.question: A financial services firm is deploying Copilot within Dynamics 365 Finance for regulatory audit workflows. The sponsor wants general LLM knowledge enabled; the CISO mandates all responses derive exclusively from validated, internally controlled content. What should the architect do?
options: A. Restrict general knowledge and configure Copilot to use only validated internal knowledge sources
B. Deploy Copilot in pilot mode with general knowledge enabled and monitor for compliance violations
C. Escalate to the business sponsor to obtain executive approval before enabling LLM-based knowledge
D. Enable general knowledge to improve natural language flexibility for auditors
questions.explanation: Restrict to validated internal knowledge sources to meet the CISO's regulatory mandate.
questions.topic: Grounding / Compliance

questions.question: [Case Study - CHG] You are designing a Field Service Routing solution that retrieves technician data from Dynamics 365, uses HIPAA-sensitive patient location data, triggers workflows via Power Automate, and escalates complex cases to supervisors. Which design decisions are appropriate? (Select ALL that apply)
options: A. Separate agents based on security boundaries (patient data vs operations)
B. Host all models in isolated compute environments by default
C. Design a sequential workflow for controlled end-to-end processing
D. Use parallel processing where independent data retrieval tasks exist
E. Use a single agent to manage all operations and simplify architecture
questions.explanation: Separate by security boundary, use sequential control flow, and parallelize independent retrieval. Isolating all models by default is over-engineering; a single agent for everything violates boundary separation.
questions.topic: Solution Design / Multi-Agent

questions.question: A healthcare organization is beginning its AI adoption journey using the Cloud Adoption Framework. Leadership agreed on high-level objectives (improve patient satisfaction, reduce administrative workload) but has not identified specific AI use cases or assessed data quality. What is the NEXT step the architect should take?
options: A. Establish program governance and Responsible AI standards before proceeding
B. Assess AI feasibility by evaluating data quality, security, and model appropriateness
C. Immediately begin configuring Copilot Studio agents for appointment scheduling
D. Identify measurable AI scenarios with high feasibility and high business impact
questions.explanation: After objectives are set, identify measurable AI scenarios with high feasibility and business impact.
questions.topic: Cloud Adoption Framework / AI

questions.question: A new AI Copilot agent for case summarization in Dynamics 365 Customer Service has passed DEV and TEST validation. The product owner pushes for direct PROD deployment to meet a customer launch deadline. The UAT/PRE-PROD environment has not been used in this release cycle. What should the architect do FIRST?
options: A. Export the managed solution package and push it to PROD via Azure DevOps with monitoring alerts enabled
B. Deploy to PROD immediately and use post-deployment telemetry to catch issues
C. Re-run regression tests in the DEV environment using production data to save time
D. Stage the agent in PRE-PROD for final business acceptance, performance, safety, and compliance validation before deploying to PROD
questions.explanation: Stage in PRE-PROD for final acceptance/performance/safety/compliance validation before PROD.
questions.topic: ALM / Release Pipeline

questions.question: A healthcare organization in the EU plans to deploy a patient-facing AI assistant for appointment booking and health FAQs. Legal flags GDPR obligations and the EU AI Act as potentially applicable. The sponsor wants to skip the regulatory review to accelerate the timeline. What should the architect do FIRST?
options: A. Deploy to a non-EU region to avoid EU AI Act compliance obligations.
B. Conduct a regulatory evaluation across applicable jurisdictions before finalizing the architecture.
C. Implement Azure AI Content Safety and assume it covers all regulatory requirements.
D. Proceed with deployment since the agent only retrieves public FAQs and poses minimal risk.
questions.explanation: Conduct a regulatory evaluation across applicable jurisdictions before finalizing architecture.
questions.topic: Compliance / Regulatory

questions.question: TRUE or FALSE: "Microsoft 365 agents can be configured with elevated admin-level access to override SharePoint security boundaries and retrieve content on behalf of all users, regardless of their individual permissions."
options: A. True
B. False
questions.explanation: Agents cannot override SharePoint security boundaries; they honor the requesting user's permissions.
questions.topic: Security / Permissions

questions.question: A financial services firm needs an AI agent that executes multi-step loan approval workflows, integrates with three internal APIs, and enforces strict separation of duties between teams. Compliance requires full auditability of every agent action, and IT has strong developer expertise. Which platform architecture decision best satisfies all constraints?
options: A. Use GPUs and containers to host a custom model for maximum compliance isolation.
B. Build using Microsoft Foundry with role-scoped agents, explicit action boundaries, evaluation pipelines, and audit trails.
C. Use Microsoft 365 Copilot (SaaS) as a productivity-first approach, minimizing customization effort.
D. Deploy using Copilot Studio with prebuilt connectors, relying on its built-in safety filters for compliance.
questions.explanation: Microsoft Foundry with role-scoped agents, explicit action boundaries, eval pipelines, and audit trails meets separation-of-duties and auditability.
questions.topic: Platform Selection / Foundry

questions.question: A global enterprise deploys a SharePoint-based Copilot agent for cross-departmental policy guidance. Each department maintains its own SharePoint site with restricted access. A business leader requests the agent be granted global read permissions via a service account so it can serve all employees regardless of their access levels. What architectural boundary must the architect enforce?
options: A. Enable agent-level admin override so the agent can bypass SharePoint permission boundaries
B. Use a custom API connector to route all content queries through a centralized knowledge repository with elevated access
C. Configure a service account with global read permissions to enable uniform cross-department access
D. Enforce that agents inherit the requesting user's permissions and cannot access content the user cannot access
questions.explanation: Agents must inherit the requesting user's permissions and cannot access content the user cannot access.
questions.topic: Security / Permissions

questions.question: (Restrict-to-internal-knowledge scenario; full option set was not captured during the attempt.) The selected answer during the attempt was to restrict general knowledge to validated internal sources.
options: A. Restrict general knowledge and configure Copilot to use only validated internal knowledge sources
questions.explanation: NOTE: Options for Q46 were not fully captured during the attempt; only the selected answer is recorded. Verify against the source. The answer aligns with the internal-only grounding guidance seen in Q38/Q54.
questions.topic: Grounding / Compliance

questions.question: An organization's AI CoE was established 18 months ago with a centralized model, approving every AI project and owning all delivery. Business units now complain about delays. The CoE has successfully standardized governance frameworks and published reusable AI templates that product teams have adopted. What is the most appropriate NEXT step for the CoE's operating model evolution?
options: A. Transition to a hybrid or advisory CoE model, where product teams take ownership of delivery while the CoE maintains standards and acts as a consultant.
B. Dissolve the CoE entirely, as product teams are now self-sufficient.
C. Expand the CoE team to handle the increased demand from business units.
D. Maintain the centralized model — it ensures consistent governance and prevents ungoverned AI adoption.
questions.explanation: Evolve from centralized to hybrid/advisory: product teams own delivery, CoE maintains standards and consults.
questions.topic: AI CoE / Operating Model

questions.question: A retail organization wants to give warehouse staff access to demand planning insights through Copilot. Staff rarely leave the operational workspace view. Two options are under discussion: a sidecar Copilot experience or an embedded AI approach. Which AI experience model best fits this scenario, and why?
options: A. Sidecar Copilot — because it supports natural language chat and is easier to configure
B. Embedded AI — because it surfaces insights directly within the workspace, reducing navigation overhead
C. External orchestration — because it allows cross-application automation
D. Sidecar Copilot — because it supports workflow summaries across modules using standardized entity metadata
questions.explanation: Embedded AI surfaces insights within the operational workspace, reducing navigation overhead for staff who rarely leave that view.
questions.topic: AI Experience Model

questions.question: A retail enterprise wants to deploy an AI agent for product recommendations across 50,000 daily customers. The CTO demands a 3-week go-live. The data engineering team warns that product catalog data is outdated, inconsistently labeled, and spread across three legacy systems. As the architect, what is the FIRST action you should take?
options: A. Defer the agent launch and mandate a data quality remediation effort, as agent reliability depends on grounding data quality and freshness.
B. Deploy the agent using Azure AI Foundry with private networking to handle the complexity of multiple data sources.
C. Build a custom SLM trained on historical product data to compensate for data quality gaps.
D. Begin building the agent in Copilot Studio immediately, as it supports rapid deployment and can be refined post-launch.
questions.explanation: Agent reliability depends on grounding data quality/freshness; defer launch and remediate data first.
questions.topic: Data Readiness

questions.question: Statement: "For a high-volume enterprise workflow automation scenario that requires dynamic AI-driven insights, developer extensibility, and automated suggestions, combining generative pages, agent feed, and code-first enhancements is a recommended architectural pattern."
options: A. True
B. False
questions.explanation: Combining generative pages, agent feed, and code-first enhancements is a recommended pattern for this scenario.
questions.topic: Architecture Patterns

questions.question: During a monthly operations review, the architect notices a significant spike in guardrail intervention events for a deployed customer service agent over the past two weeks. User satisfaction scores have declined, and several conversations were abandoned after the guardrail blocked responses. The operations manager recommends temporarily disabling guardrails. What is the MOST appropriate diagnostic step?
options: A. Expand the knowledge base by adding more documents to broaden agent response coverage
B. Roll back the agent to its previous release version immediately
C. Disable guardrails temporarily to resume normal service and restore satisfaction scores quickly
D. Analyze telemetry for guardrail trigger patterns and review conversation transcripts to identify whether guardrails are misconfigured or legitimately blocking risk
questions.explanation: Analyze telemetry and transcripts to determine whether guardrails are misconfigured or correctly blocking risk before acting.
questions.topic: Operations / Guardrails

questions.question: A retail enterprise is deploying a production Copilot agent connecting to multiple Azure-hosted backend services. The dev team embedded service principal credentials directly into the agent's configuration files. The security architect raises concerns about credential rotation and secret exposure; the team argues encrypting the config files is sufficient. What is the best approach?
options: A. Encrypt the configuration files using AES-256 and restrict file access to production admins only
B. Store credentials in Azure Key Vault and reference them dynamically from the agent configuration
C. Replace embedded secrets with managed identities for agent-to-Azure authentication to remove secrets entirely and simplify rotation
D. Rotate the embedded credentials every 30 days using an automated Key Vault script
questions.explanation: Managed identities remove stored secrets entirely and simplify rotation — the most secure option.
questions.topic: Security / Identity

questions.question: Statement: "A custom connector built in Power Automate can be created in any Power Platform environment, including the default environment, as long as the correct OpenAPI definition and OAuth 2.0 authentication are configured."
options: A. True
B. False
questions.explanation: Custom connectors can be created in any environment (including the default) with a valid OpenAPI definition and OAuth 2.0 auth.
questions.topic: Power Platform / Connectors

questions.question: A retail company is deploying an AI agent for customer collections summaries in Dynamics 365 Finance. The CFO also wants the agent to answer general regulatory finance questions using LLM capabilities. The architect has not yet completed a risk assessment for LLM enablement in this regulated environment. How should the architect advise the CFO?
options: A. Delay general knowledge enablement until risks are formally assessed and mitigated; keep the agent restricted to validated internal knowledge in the interim
B. Build a custom Azure OpenAI model to handle regulatory questions separately and bypass the governance review
C. Enable general knowledge immediately — the productivity gains outweigh the risk
D. Enable general knowledge in production and configure a compliance review process post-deployment
questions.explanation: Delay general-knowledge enablement until risks are assessed/mitigated; keep to validated internal knowledge in the interim.
questions.topic: Grounding / Risk Assessment

questions.question: TRUE or FALSE: "Storing encrypted service principal credentials in Azure Key Vault is an acceptable substitute for managed identities when securing AI agent-to-Azure authentication in an enterprise AI deployment."
options: A. True
B. False
questions.explanation: Managed identities (no stored secrets) are the preferred practice; Key Vault-stored credentials are not an equivalent substitute.
questions.topic: Security / Identity

questions.question: [Case Study - CHG] You are designing the Claims Summarization Agent. The solution requires transformation of inconsistent data from Azure Data Lake, HIPAA-compliant audit logging at the data level, and integration with custom data pipelines. The team suggests Copilot Studio for faster delivery. Which is the best platform choice to accomplish all requirements?
options: A. Microsoft Foundry to support custom pipelines and compliance controls
B. Copilot Studio with Azure AI Search for faster deployment
C. Containerized model deployment to isolate workloads
D. Microsoft 365 Copilot because it provides built-in retrieval
questions.explanation: Custom pipelines + data-level HIPAA audit logging + data transformation require Microsoft Foundry.
questions.topic: Platform Selection / Foundry

questions.question: (Repeat scenario) Warehouse staff rarely leave the operational workspace view and need demand planning insights through Copilot. Which AI experience model best fits, and why?
options: A. Sidecar Copilot — because it supports workflow summaries across modules using standardized entity metadata
B. Embedded AI — because it surfaces insights directly within the workspace, reducing navigation overhead
C. Sidecar Copilot — because it supports natural language chat and is easier to configure
D. External orchestration — because it allows cross-application automation
questions.explanation: Embedded AI surfaces insights in-workspace (duplicate of Q48 with reordered options).
questions.topic: AI Experience Model

questions.question: A financial services firm is scheduled for a production go-live of a new AI loan advisory agent. Reviewing the AI Release Readiness Checklist, the architect discovers prompts have not been regression tested and monitoring dashboards have not been configured. The CTO demands deployment by end of day to support a high-visibility client demo. What should the architect do?
options: A. Delay the production release until prompts are regression tested and monitoring dashboards are operational, regardless of the demo deadline
B. Deploy to PROD since the demo is read-only and production data will not be modified
C. Deploy to PROD and manually shadow-monitor the agent session live during the demo
D. Deploy to PROD with the demo user operating under restricted permissions and complete the checklist next week
questions.explanation: Delay release until regression testing and monitoring dashboards are complete, regardless of the demo deadline.
questions.topic: Release Readiness

questions.question: [Case Study - CHG] The CTO requests deployment of four AI agents within 90 days. CHG lacks an AI CoE, has no governance framework, and handles HIPAA-regulated patient data. You must recommend the first agent to deploy to demonstrate measurable business value while minimizing implementation and compliance risk. Which agent should you prioritize?
options: A. Claims Summarization Agent, because it processes the highest volume of data
B. Field Service Routing Agent, because it introduces multi-agent orchestration capabilities
C. HR Policy Q&A Agent, because it uses existing Microsoft 365 data with minimal compliance risk
D. Patient Intake Orchestration Agent, because it directly impacts patient operations
questions.explanation: HR Policy Q&A uses existing M365 data with minimal compliance risk — best first agent to show value while minimizing risk.
questions.topic: Use Case Prioritization

questions.question: An insurance company preparing to launch an AI agent for claims triage discovers during a Responsible AI review that the fairness assessment reveals statistically different outcomes for similar claim profiles from different demographic groups. The product owner wants to launch on schedule and address the bias in a post-launch patch. What should the architect recommend?
options: A. Delay the launch until the fairness issue is identified, root-caused, and mitigated — Fairness is a core Responsible AI principle that must be satisfied before deployment
B. Launch to a limited pilot group and use production telemetry to quantify the bias before patching
C. Launch on schedule but add a disclaimer that the agent's recommendations are AI-generated and subject to change
D. Replace the AI agent with a manual rules-based triage system to eliminate bias risk entirely
questions.explanation: Fairness must be satisfied before deployment; delay until the bias is root-caused and mitigated.
questions.topic: Responsible AI / Fairness

questions.question: A service organization uses the term "red account" for a customer that has a critical service tier and at least one unresolved priority case. Representatives want Customer Service Copilot summaries to use this term consistently. What should the solution architect recommend?
options: A. Add the phrase to the agent instructions without identifying the underlying records
B. Define the term in business language, map it to the authoritative fields and relationships, and test it with representative records
C. Rename the Account table to Red Account so Copilot can recognize the term
D. Give Copilot access to every Dataverse table so it can infer the meaning
questions.explanation: Define organization-specific terms precisely and map them to authoritative records, fields, and relationships. Summary configuration supports natural-language descriptions and explicit field selection while preserving existing access controls.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Dynamics 365 business terms and grounding

questions.question: Customer service representatives need case summaries with separate Issue, Actions Taken, and Next Step sections. Empty sections must not appear when a case lacks the corresponding data. Which configuration best meets the requirement?
options: A. Select Paragraph format and increase summary verbosity
B. Select Structured format, configure custom headers, and enable removal of information that cannot be found
C. Add all case fields to a paragraph summary and ask representatives to ignore missing values
D. Create a separate custom table for each summary section
questions.explanation: Structured format supports custom headers, and removing information that cannot be found prevents empty sections or placeholder text when source data is unavailable.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Customer Service summary customization

questions.question: Representatives viewing a case should see summaries of its related work orders, with the most recently modified work order first and its work-order number displayed as the heading. What should the architect configure?
options: A. Add Work Order as an unrelated knowledge source and sort the generated text afterward
B. Include related records, use the Work Order field that references the parent case, prioritize by Modified Date, and display Work Order Number
C. Copy every work order into the case description through a nightly batch process
D. Configure only a 1-to-1 relationship between Case and Work Order
questions.explanation: Related-record summaries require the related record type, parent-reference field, summary configuration, ordering field, and heading field.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Related-record summary design

questions.question: An administrator includes Product in a case-summary configuration, but summaries generated for service representatives omit product information. The field is populated on the cases. What should the architect verify first?
options: A. Whether representatives have the required read privilege for Product and the related entities
B. Whether the representatives have System Administrator access to the entire environment
C. Whether Product was copied into an unauthenticated public knowledge source
D. Whether the summary uses Paragraph rather than Structured format
questions.explanation: Customer Service summaries respect Dataverse privileges. Verify the required read access to Product and related entities rather than granting broad administrative access.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Customer Service permissions and summaries

questions.question: A company wants sellers to view opportunity summaries in Outlook and Teams. One division uses Dynamics 365 Sales and another uses Salesforce Sales Cloud. Which packaged experience is the best fit under current Microsoft naming?
options: A. Service Agent
B. Sales Agent
C. Dynamics 365 Contact Center voice agent
D. A custom Customer Service record-summary control
questions.explanation: Sales Agent brings CRM insights into Outlook, Teams, and Microsoft 365 apps and supports connections to Dynamics 365 Sales and Salesforce Sales Cloud.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Sales Agent and CRM connections

questions.question: A seller was granted permission in the CRM to update opportunities, but Sales Agent in Outlook still prevents the update immediately after the role change. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: A. Configure Sales Agent to bypass CRM authorization
B. Assign a shared system-administrator identity to all sellers
C. Have the seller sign out of Sales Agent in Outlook and sign in again so the changed CRM permissions are reflected
D. Replace the CRM connection with an anonymous custom connector
questions.explanation: Sales Agent applies CRM access controls. After CRM permission or security-role changes, the Outlook user should sign out of Sales Agent and sign in again.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Sales Agent permissions

questions.question: An architecture document written in 2025 refers to "Microsoft 365 Copilot for Sales." A current implementation guide refers to "Sales Agent." How should the architect interpret the terms for an AB-100 scenario?
options: A. They always identify unrelated products with incompatible CRM sources
B. Sales Agent is the current documentation name for the seller-focused experience formerly described as Microsoft 365 Copilot for Sales
C. Sales Agent refers only to an autonomous agent built in Copilot Studio
D. Microsoft 365 Copilot for Sales is the current name, and Sales Agent is retired terminology
questions.explanation: Current Microsoft Learn documentation uses Sales Agent for the seller-focused Microsoft 365 experience. Older exam material can use Microsoft 365 Copilot for Sales or similar legacy names.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Product terminology

questions.question: A seller asks an agent, "Summarize this opportunity and identify the documented risks." The agent retrieves permitted CRM data, returns an answer, and makes no record changes. Which agent type best describes the design?
options: A. Prompt and response agent
B. Task agent
C. Autonomous agent
D. Event-processing agent flow
questions.explanation: The interaction begins with a user prompt and produces an informational response without carrying out a bounded operational workflow.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Prompt and response agents

questions.question: A seller selects Prepare Meeting Brief. The agent retrieves the account and opportunity, summarizes recent meetings, drafts an agenda, and creates a follow-up task. It runs only when the seller invokes this bounded operation. Which classification is most appropriate?
options: A. Prompt and response agent, because all agents receive some input
B. Task agent, because it completes an explicitly invoked multistep goal with tools
C. Autonomous agent, because it uses more than one tool
D. Knowledge-only agent, because the first step retrieves records
questions.explanation: A task agent completes a bounded goal and can invoke multiple tools. Tool use alone does not make an agent autonomous.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Task agents

questions.question: A new high-priority Customer Service case should automatically start triage when its Dataverse record is created. The agent may collect context and recommend an escalation, but changing a customer's contractual service level requires manager approval. Which design is best?
options: A. Use a prompt and response agent and rely on a representative to notice every new case
B. Use an autonomous event trigger for triage and place the contractual change behind a deterministic approval boundary
C. Give the autonomous agent unrestricted write access so the workflow never pauses
D. Use a task agent with a scheduled prompt entered manually by an administrator
questions.explanation: A record-created event can start autonomous work without a user message, while consequential changes should remain behind deterministic controls or human approval.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Autonomous agents and approval boundaries

questions.question: A customer enters an utterance that matches no enabled topic in a classic-orchestration agent. The architect wants the standard unknown-intent behavior with a bounded retry before handoff. Which design should be used?
options: A. Add broad trigger phrases to every business topic and let the highest-priority topic guess the intent
B. Use the Fallback system topic with On Unknown Intent, ask for rephrasing no more than twice, and then redirect to Escalate
C. Create a prompt action that always generates an answer from unrestricted public knowledge
D. Configure Multiple Topics Matched to run whenever no topic is eligible
questions.explanation: The Fallback system topic catches unrecognized input through On Unknown Intent. Its documented default path asks the user to rephrase no more than twice and then redirects to the Escalate system topic.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Fallback and escalation

questions.question: An architect adds a topic named General Help with trigger phrases such as help, problem, and question. Analytics then show that specific billing and order topics rarely run. What is the best correction?
options: A. Give General Help the highest trigger priority so its behavior is consistent
B. Add more generic phrases to General Help to improve its recognition coverage
C. Remove the catchall trigger phrases and let the Fallback system topic handle unmatched input before bounded clarification or escalation
D. Disable the specific topics and implement all conversations in General Help
questions.explanation: Fallback already captures unknown content without trigger phrases. A broad catchall topic can steal traffic from valid topics and conceal recognition gaps instead of exposing them for correction.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Topic design and fallback traps

questions.question: A benefits agent has 12 stable intents, must present approved wording, and must follow an authored sequence for each intent. Which orchestration design best fits?
options: A. Classic orchestration with User says a phrase triggers and semantically varied phrases for each topic
B. Generative orchestration with overlapping topic descriptions so the planner can choose several paths
C. CLU solely because the agent contains more than ten intents
D. A scheduled agent flow with no conversational topics
questions.explanation: Classic orchestration selects topics by matching user input to trigger phrases and is the better fit for a small, stable intent set that requires predictable authored dialogue and ordering.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Classic orchestration and standard NLU

questions.question: An employee asks, 'Find my leave balance, explain the carryover policy, and draft a message to my manager.' The solution has a balance tool, an approved policy knowledge source, and a drafting prompt. Which design best supports the request?
options: A. Classic orchestration with one trigger phrase and no explicit tool inputs
B. Generative orchestration with distinct capability descriptions and input/output contracts so the agent can select and sequence the tool, knowledge, and prompt
C. CLU with one intent named EmployeeRequest and no mapped entities
D. Fallback that sends the entire request directly to an escalation queue
questions.explanation: Generative orchestration can combine topics, tools, knowledge, and other capabilities for a multi-intent request. Clear descriptions and parameter contracts help the planner select and sequence the correct capabilities.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Generative orchestration and capability contracts

questions.question: A telecom support team has hundreds of labeled utterances, a controlled taxonomy of contract and product intents, domain-specific entities, and an ML team that must measure and version recognition performance. Which recognition approach is most appropriate?
options: A. Continue adding generic trigger phrases indefinitely because external models cannot provide entities
B. Integrate a trained and deployed Azure AI Language CLU model, map its intents to topics, and use its imported entities
C. Replace intent recognition with a prompt that writes directly to the billing system
D. Use the Fallback topic as the primary recognizer for all supported requests
questions.explanation: CLU is appropriate when a specialized domain needs a trained intent and entity model with labeled data, measurable recognition, deployment, and version management. Copilot Studio can map CLU intents to topics and use imported entities.
questions.topic: D2.1 / CLU selection and lifecycle

questions.question: A generatively orchestrated topic requires a value that must match a custom regex entity for an internal asset tag. The maker tries to define that custom entity directly as the topic input parameter. What should the architect recommend?
options: A. Keep the custom entity as a direct parameter because all entity types are supported by generative orchestration
B. Collect the asset tag with a Question node that uses the custom entity, then pass the validated value onward
C. Remove validation and let the planner infer any missing asset tag
D. Convert the regex entity into a broad fallback trigger phrase
questions.explanation: Generative topic and tool input parameters don't directly support custom closed-list or regex entities. The documented approach is to collect the value with a Question node in a topic.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Generative orchestration input limitations

questions.question: A refund process must check eligibility, branch on amount, retry a transient ERP call, obtain manager approval above a threshold, and then update the ERP. A model may summarize the case but must not decide the threshold. Where should the core process be implemented?
options: A. In one prompt action whose natural-language instructions describe all approval rules
B. In an agent flow with deterministic branches, retries, connectors, and approval actions; use a prompt only as a bounded summarization step
C. In the Fallback system topic so unknown refund requests can write to the ERP
D. In overlapping generative topic descriptions so the planner can choose the approval threshold
questions.explanation: Agent flows are the appropriate boundary for deterministic process logic, connectors, retries, approvals, and side effects. A prompt can assist with semantic transformation but should not own consequential business rules.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Agent flows and deterministic control

questions.question: A maker builds an agent flow that looks up shipment status. The flow must be available for a generatively orchestrated agent to select as a tool and must return a typed status result. Which configuration is required?
options: A. Use When an agent calls the flow, define clear inputs and outputs, and add the flow as an agent tool with a precise description
B. Use only a recurrence trigger and infer the requesting user's order from flow run history
C. Use On Unknown Intent and omit outputs because the planner reads connector logs
D. Use User says a phrase inside the flow and store the result in a global variable
questions.explanation: Agent flows with the When an agent calls the flow trigger can be added as tools. Clear input/output contracts and a precise description enable reliable selection and data exchange.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Agent flow tool contracts

questions.question: An agent must retrieve an approved email, extract category and urgency into a strict schema, validate the result, and create a Dataverse case only after a representative confirms it. Which architecture is best?
options: A. A prompt performs extraction and writes the case immediately because structured output guarantees correctness
B. An agent flow retrieves the email, runs a prompt for bounded extraction, validates the output, obtains confirmation, and then writes the case
C. A classic topic stores the unvalidated model response directly in Dataverse without a flow
D. CLU performs the connector write because entity recognition includes transaction handling
questions.explanation: The prompt is suited to semantic extraction, while the agent flow owns retrieval, validation, confirmation, persistence, and failure handling. Structured model output still requires validation before a consequential write.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Prompt actions composed with agent flows

questions.question: A custom prompt classifies incoming complaints and returns valid JSON during testing. The product owner argues that temperature 0 and valid JSON make further controls unnecessary. What should the architect recommend?
options: A. Accept the design because temperature 0 guarantees identical and factual output
B. Validate the schema and allowed values, test representative and adversarial inputs, handle insufficient information, and require review before high-impact actions
C. Increase temperature so incorrect classifications are easier to detect
D. Move the classification into fallback because fallback output is deterministic
questions.explanation: Prompt output remains probabilistic even with low temperature and structured formatting. Validate the output contract, test edge cases, define an insufficient-information path, and keep human or deterministic controls around consequential actions.
questions.topic: D2.1 / Prompt action validation and safety

questions.question: A company is building an employee policy agent. Policy documents change every week, responses must reflect the latest approved version, and users should receive citations. The base model already follows instructions adequately. Which approach should the architect recommend?
options: A. Fine-tune the model whenever a policy document changes
B. Train a new foundation model on the complete policy archive
C. Ground the agent through retrieval over the approved policy repository
D. Add more policy excerpts permanently to the system prompt
questions.explanation: Retrieval grounding is appropriate when authoritative knowledge changes frequently and must be cited. It supplies current information at run time without changing model weights. Fine-tuning is better suited to changing behavior, style, format, or task performance.
questions.topic: D2.2 / Foundry model customization versus RAG

questions.question: A claims team has optimized its prompts, but the model still produces inconsistent JSON for numerous edge cases. The team has 2,000 reviewed prompt-response examples that demonstrate the required schema and behavior. The underlying business facts are supplied separately at run time. What is the best next step?
options: A. Fine-tune a supported model with the reviewed examples and evaluate it against a held-out test set
B. Replace the reviewed examples with a larger retrieval index
C. Add a Computer Use tool so the model can learn the output schema
D. Move every example into the system prompt for each request
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning is suitable when a high-quality task-specific dataset is available and the objective is more consistent behavior, formatting, or handling of many edge cases. Retrieval supplies knowledge but does not by itself train consistent schema behavior.
questions.topic: D2.2 / Fine-tuning decision boundaries

questions.question: A support agent can explain return policies correctly, but it must now create a return authorization in a line-of-business system that exposes a secured API. Which extension should the architect select?
options: A. Fine-tune the model with examples of successful return authorizations
B. Add the system's API as a tool or action with appropriate authentication
C. Index historical return authorizations as a knowledge source
D. Use a deep reasoning model without adding an integration
questions.explanation: Creating a record in an external system is an action with side effects, so the agent needs an authenticated tool that invokes the API. Grounding and fine-tuning do not independently provide authority or connectivity to perform the transaction.
questions.topic: D2.2 / Tools versus grounding and fine-tuning

questions.question: A Copilot Studio agent must use a standards-based server that exposes several tools and resources. The available operations will evolve over time, and the agent should select the appropriate operation from the user's intent. Which design best meets the requirement?
options: A. Connect the MCP server as an agent tool and use generative orchestration
B. Copy every MCP resource into a static prompt and use classic orchestration
C. Create one hard-coded topic for every possible natural-language request
D. Fine-tune a model on the MCP server's tool names
questions.explanation: Copilot Studio can connect to an MCP server to access dynamically advertised tools and resources. MCP requires generative orchestration so the agent can select the appropriate capability.
questions.topic: D2.2 / Copilot Studio MCP and generative orchestration

questions.question: An agent must enter data into a legacy desktop application. The application has no API or supported connector, and completing the process requires clicking controls and typing into visible fields. Which capability and prerequisite should the architect identify?
options: A. Computer Use with generative orchestration enabled
B. An MCP resource with classic orchestration enabled
C. SharePoint grounding with semantic search enabled
D. Model fine-tuning with desktop screenshots as training data
questions.explanation: Computer Use is intended for web or desktop GUI automation when an API is unavailable. It interacts through visible controls using mouse and keyboard actions and requires generative orchestration.
questions.topic: D2.2 / Computer Use selection

questions.question: A Computer Use agent will be shared with employees whose permissions in the target application differ by role. The organization must avoid having every execution inherit the maker's access and wants execution to stop for review when potentially harmful instructions are detected. What should the architect configure?
options: A. Maker-provided credentials and disable supervision to prevent timeouts
B. One shared administrator account stored directly in the agent instructions
C. End-user credentials and human supervision with an appropriate response time limit
D. Anonymous access combined with a SharePoint sensitivity label
questions.explanation: End-user credentials preserve each user's access boundary instead of running with the maker's permissions. Human supervision can stop potentially harmful instructions for review, with a configured response time limit.
questions.topic: D2.2 / Computer Use identity, security, and supervision

questions.question: An agent must compare several complex contract documents, reconcile conflicting clauses, and construct a defensible recommendation. Interactive latency is less important than analytical quality. Which model choice is most appropriate?
options: A. A realtime audio model because it minimizes speech latency
B. A reasoning model, while allowing for additional processing time and reasoning-token usage
C. A Computer Use model because contracts are unstructured
D. A text-to-speech model with a longer system prompt
questions.explanation: Reasoning models are suited to advanced problem solving and complex document comparison. They can spend additional time and reasoning tokens processing a request, so they fit when analytical quality matters more than immediate latency.
questions.topic: D2.2 / Deep reasoning model selection

questions.question: A company is designing a browser-based voice assistant that must listen and respond with low latency during a live conversation. Which architecture best aligns with the Microsoft Foundry Realtime API guidance?
options: A. Use a realtime audio model over WebRTC and provide a client integration that terminates the user's audio stream
B. Upload the completed recording to a reasoning model after each conversation
C. Connect the Realtime API directly to the user's microphone without a client integration
D. Fine-tune a text model and poll it periodically for synthesized audio
questions.explanation: The Realtime API supports low-latency speech-in, speech-out interaction. WebRTC is recommended for most client-side realtime audio scenarios, with a client integration terminating and relaying the user's audio stream.
questions.topic: D2.2 / Realtime voice selection and limitations

questions.question: A Copilot Studio maker publishes an agent and connects it to Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot. The business now wants every employee to discover it in the Teams app store under Built for your org. What additional step is required?
options: A. Add the publishing link to a SharePoint page
B. Fine-tune the agent before organizational distribution
C. Submit the agent for administrator approval for organizational availability
D. Assign every employee as a co-owner of the agent
questions.explanation: Publishing and connecting channels do not automatically place the agent in the organization-wide store. An agent intended for Built for your org must be submitted for administrator approval.
questions.topic: D2.2 / Teams and Microsoft 365 Copilot distribution

questions.question: An Agent Builder agent in Microsoft 365 Copilot is grounded in a SharePoint site containing both general procedures and restricted legal documents. The owner enables organization-wide chat access. What should the architect expect when an employee without permission to the legal documents uses the agent?
options: A. The employee can receive content from every file because organization-wide sharing overrides SharePoint permissions
B. The employee can receive restricted content if the agent owner can access it
C. The employee can access restricted content after accepting the agent's sharing link
D. The agent continues to respect the employee's existing SharePoint permissions and sensitivity-label boundaries
questions.explanation: Sharing or making an agent discoverable does not grant access to its underlying SharePoint content. SharePoint and OneDrive knowledge sources continue to respect existing permissions and sensitivity labels.
questions.topic: D2.2 / SharePoint grounding and permission boundaries

questions.question: Finance users need contextual in-app guidance based on Microsoft's current public documentation, plus the company's approved operating procedures in SharePoint. What should the architect recommend?
options: A. Replace the finance and operations Copilot sidecar with a fine-tuned model
B. Use generative help and guidance, then extend its knowledge in Copilot Studio with the approved SharePoint source
C. Copy all procedures into each user's personal prompt library
D. Use Supplier Communications Agent because it indexes all finance documentation
questions.explanation: Generative help and guidance provides the contextual finance and operations sidecar grounded in Microsoft public documentation. Administrators can extend it in Copilot Studio with files or sources such as SharePoint.
questions.topic: D2.3 / Finance and operations generative help knowledge

questions.question: A custom Copilot Studio agent must answer questions about live structured purchase-order data in finance and operations apps while respecting the data available to the user. Which design is appropriate?
options: A. Add finance and operations virtual entities as a knowledge source
B. Export monthly screenshots and add them as image knowledge
C. Fine-tune the model on old purchase orders
D. Enable unrestricted general model knowledge
questions.explanation: Finance and operations virtual entities can expose structured ERP data as a Copilot Studio knowledge source. A native Dataverse table populated through a synchronization mechanism such as dual-write is another supported pattern.
questions.topic: D2.3 / Structured finance and operations knowledge

questions.question: Employees want to ask questions about approved ERP data directly from Microsoft 365 Copilot rather than opening Dynamics 365. What should the architect propose?
options: A. Create a declarative agent with the finance and operations knowledge and required actions, then publish it to Microsoft 365 Copilot
B. Grant Microsoft 365 Copilot direct database-owner access
C. Add ERP records to every employee's mailbox
D. Use only the default public-documentation grounding in the finance sidecar
questions.explanation: Microsoft Learn recommends a declarative agent when extending Microsoft 365 Copilot with finance and operations knowledge. The agent packages the approved knowledge and actions and is then published to Microsoft 365 Copilot.
questions.topic: D2.3 / Microsoft 365 agent for ERP scenarios

questions.question: A procurement team spends significant time following up with vendors, updating purchase orders, and managing change requests according to user-defined rules. Which prebuilt capability is the closest fit?
options: A. Collections coordinator summary
B. Supplier Communications Agent in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
C. Microsoft 365 Agent Builder coaching agent
D. Dynamics 365 Customer Service case summary
questions.explanation: Supplier Communications Agent targets repetitive procure-to-pay collaboration, including vendor follow-up, purchase-order updates, and change-request handling based on configured rules.
questions.topic: D2.3 / Supply Chain prebuilt agents

questions.question: A collections manager wants AI-generated customer context in the Collections coordinator workspace and assistance drafting reminder letters. Which Dynamics 365 capability should be evaluated first?
options: A. Collections coordinator summary in Dynamics 365 Finance
B. Supplier Communications Agent
C. Computer Use in Copilot Studio
D. Dynamics 365 Sales relationship intelligence
questions.explanation: Collections coordinator summary provides AI-generated summary text in the Collections coordinator workspace and can generate reminder letters containing AI-generated text.
questions.topic: D2.3 / Dynamics 365 Finance AI features

questions.question: An architect needs the same model-driven AI capability, such as record summaries, across Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service. Why should Power Apps capabilities be considered?
options: A. Sales and Customer Service are model-driven apps built on Power Apps and can inherit supported Power Apps AI capabilities
B. Power Apps automatically replaces all Dynamics 365 security roles
C. Power Apps converts every CRM record into public web knowledge
D. Power Apps is required only for finance and operations batch jobs
questions.explanation: Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service are model-driven Power Apps. Supported Power Apps capabilities such as record summaries, form-fill assistance, data discovery, and visualization can therefore surface in those apps.
questions.topic: D2.3 / Power Apps AI in Dynamics 365 customer apps

questions.question: A seller needs CRM-aware assistance in Outlook and Teams, while a service representative needs case and knowledge assistance for resolving customer issues. What is the correct product alignment?
options: A. Microsoft 365 Copilot for Sales for the seller, and Microsoft 365 Copilot for Service for the service representative
B. Copilot for Service for the seller, and Supplier Communications Agent for the service representative
C. Collections coordinator summary for both users
D. Power BI Copilot for the seller, and Microsoft 365 Agent Builder for all case management
questions.explanation: Copilot for Sales connects the seller's Microsoft 365 workflow with CRM context. Copilot for Service is aimed at service representatives and brings CRM and knowledge assistance into their flow of work.
questions.topic: D2.3 / Copilot for Sales and Copilot for Service selection

questions.question: A maker wants to add document processing, prediction, and a bounded generative prompt to a Power Platform solution without building and hosting separate custom AI services. Which capability family should the architect propose?
options: A. AI Builder and the Power Platform AI capabilities surfaced through the AI hub
B. Dynamics 365 Finance collections summary only
C. Microsoft 365 Copilot public web grounding only
D. A custom foundation model for every task
questions.explanation: Power Platform AI capabilities and AI Builder provide low-code access to prebuilt or custom models and prompts that can be composed into Power Apps and Power Automate solutions.
questions.topic: D2.3 / Power Platform AI hub and AI Builder

questions.question: A finance agent can answer questions about purchase orders from a Dataverse knowledge source. The business now wants it to approve and update purchase orders. What additional design is required?
options: A. Add authenticated actions or tools with authorization, validation, and approval controls
B. Increase the number of indexed purchase orders
C. Enable general model knowledge
D. Fine-tune the model on approval emails
questions.explanation: Knowledge sources support retrieval and Q&A; they do not grant transactional authority. Updates require authenticated actions or tools plus deterministic authorization, validation, and approval controls.
questions.topic: D2.3 / Knowledge versus transactional actions

questions.question: An administrator enables custom knowledge and optional general-question answering for finance and operations generative help. In what order does Copilot use these sources?
options: A. It uses general model and web content first, then checks custom knowledge
B. It uses custom knowledge first and can use general model, Bing web, and other enabled sources after custom knowledge is exhausted
C. It randomly chooses one source for every request
D. Enabling general questions permanently disables public documentation grounding
questions.explanation: Microsoft Learn states that optional general content is used after Copilot exhausts the configured custom knowledge sources. General content can include model knowledge, Bing-identified web content, and other sources.
questions.topic: D2.3 / Finance generative-help source precedence
